1	package kokoro
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"math/rand"
6		"time"
7	)
8	
9	// Prosody is everything the vocoder needs and nothing it does not: the
10	// expanded phoneme features, the two curves that condition them, and the
11	// alignment that produced all three.
12	type Prosody struct {
13		Tokens    []int     // the input ids, boundary tokens included
14		Durations []int     // one frame count per token, summing to Frames
15		Frames    int       // alignment frames, 25 ms each
16		ASR       *Mat      // [Frames, 512], the text encoder expanded
17		Encoded   *Mat      // [Frames, 640], the duration encoder expanded
18		F0        []float32 // [2*Frames]
19		Energy    []float32 // [2*Frames]
20		RawDur    []float32 // the durations before rounding, for diagnostics
21	
22		// Where the time went. The phoneme side is 85% of an utterance and 60% of
23		// *it* is recurrences, so the split that matters is ALBERT against the six
24		// bidirectional LSTMs (SPEECH.md T6).
25		Times ProsodyTimes
26	}
27	
28	// ProsodyTimes is the phoneme side, stage by stage.
29	type ProsodyTimes struct {
30		BERT        time.Duration // 12 ALBERT layers over the tokens
31		DurEncoder  time.Duration // three LSTM/AdaLayerNorm pairs
32		Durations   time.Duration // one LSTM and the duration head
33		Prosody     time.Duration // the shared LSTM and the F0/N stacks
34		Shared      time.Duration // of Prosody: the recurrence across the regulator
35		Stacks      time.Duration // of Prosody: the six F0/N AdaIN blocks
36		TextEncoder time.Duration // an embedding, three convolutions and one LSTM
37		Expand      time.Duration // the length regulator, twice
38	}
39	
40	// Total is the whole phoneme side.
41	func (t ProsodyTimes) Total() time.Duration {
42		return t.BERT + t.DurEncoder + t.Durations + t.Prosody + t.TextEncoder + t.Expand
43	}
44	
45	// Samples is how long the waveform will be, which is fixed the moment the
46	// durations are rounded — 600 samples an alignment frame at 24 kHz.
47	func (p *Prosody) Samples(cfg *Config) int {
48		return p.Frames * cfg.SamplesPerFrame()
49	}
50	
51	// Seconds is Samples in wall-clock terms.
52	func (p *Prosody) Seconds(cfg *Config) float64 {
53		return float64(p.Samples(cfg)) / float64(cfg.SamplingRate)
54	}
55	
56	// Prosody runs everything up to the vocoder: both encoders, the duration
57	// head, the length regulator and the F0/energy stacks.
58	//
59	// The order matters and is not the order the modules are declared in. ALBERT
60	// and the duration encoder decide *how long* the utterance is before the text
61	// encoder's output can be expanded, so the cheap path (five convolutions and
62	// an LSTM over 50 frames) waits on the expensive one (twelve transformer
63	// layers). Nothing downstream of here has a shape that was known when the
64	// call started.
65	func (m *Model) Prosody(ids []int, style []float32, speed float32) (*Prosody, error) {
66		if speed <= 0 {
67			return nil, fmt.Errorf("kokoro: speed %g", speed)
68		}
69		if len(style) != m.Config.StyleDim {
70			return nil, fmt.Errorf("kokoro: predictor style is %d wide, want %d",
71				len(style), m.Config.StyleDim)
72		}
73		var times ProsodyTimes
74		t0 := time.Now()
75		var last *Mat
76		if m.BERTGPU != nil {
77			// The embedding stack stays on the host: a table lookup, two adds and
78			// a 128->768 projection over fifty rows is not worth a dispatch.
79			_, hidden, err := m.BERT.Embed(ids)
80			if err != nil {
81				return nil, err
82			}
83			if last, err = m.BERTGPU.Apply(hidden); err != nil {
84				return nil, err
85			}
86		} else {
87			hiddens, err := m.BERT.Apply(ids)
88			if err != nil {
89				return nil, err
90			}
91			last = hiddens[len(hiddens)-1]
92		}
93		dEn, err := m.BERTEncoder.Apply(last)
94		if err != nil {
95			return nil, err
96		}
97		times.BERT = time.Since(t0)
98	
99		t0 = time.Now()
100		encoded, err := m.Predictor.TextEncoder.Apply(dEn, style)
101		if err != nil {
102			return nil, err
103		}
104		times.DurEncoder = time.Since(t0)
105	
106		t0 = time.Now()
107		durations, raw, err := m.Predictor.Durations(encoded, speed)
108		if err != nil {
109			return nil, err
110		}
111		times.Durations = time.Since(t0)
112	
113		t0 = time.Now()
114		en, err := Expand(encoded, durations)
115		if err != nil {
116			return nil, err
117		}
118		times.Expand = time.Since(t0)
119	
120		t0 = time.Now()
121		f0, energy, err := m.Predictor.Prosody(en, style, &times)
122		if err != nil {
123			return nil, err
124		}
125		times.Prosody = time.Since(t0)
126	
127		t0 = time.Now()
128		tEn, err := m.TextEncoder.Apply(ids)
129		if err != nil {
130			return nil, err
131		}
132		times.TextEncoder = time.Since(t0)
133	
134		t0 = time.Now()
135		asr, err := Expand(tEn, durations)
136		if err != nil {
137			return nil, err
138		}
139		times.Expand += time.Since(t0)
140	
141		return &Prosody{
142			Tokens: ids, Durations: durations, Frames: en.Rows,
143			ASR: asr, Encoded: en, F0: f0, Energy: energy, RawDur: raw,
144			Times: times,
145		}, nil
146	}
147	
148	// Synthesize runs the whole model: phonemes in, samples out at 24 kHz.
149	//
150	// The two halves of the style vector go to different places and are not
151	// interchangeable — the predictor's 128 condition every AdaLayerNorm before
152	// the length regulator, the decoder's condition every AdaIN after it — so
153	// Style returns them in the order they are used here.
154	func (m *Model) Synthesize(ids []int, decStyle, predStyle []float32, speed float32) ([]float32, *Prosody, error) {
155		p, err := m.Prosody(ids, predStyle, speed)
156		if err != nil {
157			return nil, nil, err
158		}
159		audio, _, err := m.Vocoder.Apply(p.ASR, p.F0, p.Energy, decStyle)
160		if err != nil {
161			return nil, p, err
162		}
163		if want := p.Samples(m.Config); len(audio) != want {
164			return nil, p, fmt.Errorf("kokoro: %d samples, the durations say %d", len(audio), want)
165		}
166		return audio, p, nil
167	}
168	
169	// SetExcitationNoise switches the vocoder's excitation noise on, seeded.
170	//
171	// Off is the default because it is what the reference dump was taken with and
172	// the only configuration in which two runs agree. On is what an utterance
173	// meant to be listened to wants: see HarmonicSource.
174	func (m *Model) SetExcitationNoise(seed int64) {
175		m.Vocoder.Generator.Source.Noise = rand.New(rand.NewSource(seed))
176	}
177	
178	// Speak is Synthesize from a phoneme string and a voice name, which is the
179	// whole API the HTTP layer needs.
180	func (m *Model) Speak(phonemes, voice string, speed float32) ([]float32, *Prosody, error) {
181		ids, dropped := m.Config.Phonemes(phonemes)
182		if len(ids) <= 2 {
183			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("kokoro: no phonemes in %q", phonemes)
184		}
185		// The style row is indexed by the phoneme count the *caller* supplied,
186		// minus whatever fell outside the vocabulary — which is how KPipeline
187		// indexes it, and is not the token count.
188		dec, pred, err := m.Style(voice, len([]rune(phonemes))-dropped)
189		if err != nil {
190			return nil, nil, err
191		}
192		return m.Synthesize(ids, dec, pred, speed)
193	}

**Result: the prosody predictor's two AdaIN stacks go from 40 ms to 1 ms — and
an utterance from 156 ms to 115 ms, 20.9x real time to 28.4x. The durations
are unchanged and both curves agree with the reference dump to 2.4e-5.**

    stage          gpu    (T6a)   cpu (T3)
    bert            4ms      4ms     104ms
    dur encoder    30ms     29ms      24ms
    durations       9ms      8ms       8ms
    prosody        23ms     64ms      66ms   shared LSTM 22ms, F0/N stacks 1ms
    text encoder   17ms     16ms      15ms
    phoneme side   76ms    117ms     222ms   66% of the utterance
    vocoder        39ms     39ms    3626ms
    total         115ms    156ms    3848ms   28.35x real time, from 20.88x

**The instrument came first again, and again it moved the number.**
`SPEECH.md` had carried "~33 ms" for these stacks since T6a, inferred by
subtraction. Splitting `Prosody`'s 64 ms into the shared recurrence and the
stacks measured **24 ms and 40 ms** — the stacks are a third of the whole
phoneme side, not a quarter of the predictor. Three lines of `time.Now()`
before any kernel, and the stage is worth a quarter more than it looked.

**Almost all of the work was deleting the assumption that this needed new
code.** These six blocks are `AdainResBlk1d` — the same type `GPUDecoder` has
run since T4c, on the same eleven-dispatch graph, the same A_CONV=2 rungs, the
same bordered fp16 arena and the same two-phase AdaIN reduction. So the stage
is a **refactor plus plumbing**: `kokoro/adainset.go` lifts `decBlock`, the
weight layout, the staging, the style projection and the dispatch graph out of
`gpudec.go` into a `blockSet` both objects embed, and `kokoro/gpuprosody.go`
is the 300 lines that say where a block's input comes from and where its
output goes. **One new shader in the whole stage**, and it is nine lines of
arithmetic.

**Built:**

- `kokoro/adainset.go` — `blockSet`: the block machinery neither object owns.
  `GPUDecoder` shrank from 729 lines to 290 and its numbers did not move
  (59.1 dB against the CPU path, 18.2 dB against the dump, both unchanged).
- `kokoro/gpuprosody.go` — `GPUProsody`, six blocks and two projections over
  one fp32 arena, **62 dispatches in one submit**.
- `shaders/kokoro_proj.comp` — `F0_proj` and `N_proj`, 256 channels to one.
- `decBlock.noSC`, and a row stride of its own for `kokoro_shortcut.comp`.
- The `Shared`/`Stacks` split on `ProsodyTimes`, printed by `cmd/tts`.
- `kokoro/gpuprosody_test.go` — five tests: block by block against the dump,
  both curves against the dump *and* the CPU, the ladder, the dispatch
  profile, and the durations.

**Four things worth carrying forward:**

1. **The third shape of shortcut is no shortcut.** Four of these six blocks
   keep their channel count, so upstream builds them with `conv1x1 = None` and
   the shortcut is the block's input unchanged. On the device that is not a
   special case to implement but **three dispatches and an fp16 sub-arena that
   do not happen**: the epilogue reads the input where it already lies. It
   needed one thing — the epilogue had assumed its second operand had the
   block's own row stride, which is only true when the block made it.
2. **A 1-wide output is a kernel, not a rung.** The two projections are
   [260, 256] x [256, 1]. Every rung writes a 16-wide cooperative-matrix
   fragment, so the narrowest GEMM on offer is 16 columns of which 15 would be
   zero weight — *plus* a narrow into the fp16 arena for an operand that is
   already in fp32. A workgroup-per-frame scalar reduction is 0.0015 ms and
   exact. **Reuse is the default, but the fragment tile is a hard floor**, and
   T6a's "do not reach for the matrix cores by reflex" cuts both ways.
3. **The readback is the reason the projection is on the device at all.**
   It is 0.7% of the stacks' GPU time and could trivially have stayed on the
   host — except that the host would then need the last block's [260, 256]
   activation, and this device reads host-visible memory at 210 MB/s (T4a).
   That is 1.3 ms a curve, against 1 KB and 5 µs for the curve itself. The
   arithmetic did not move to the device; the **boundary** did.
4. **`GroupsY` defaults to zero, and a zero grid is legal.** The projection
   dispatched nothing and failed silently — every block correct to 1e-4, both
   curves exactly 0.0. Everything else in this package writes a 2-D grid, so
   this is the first 1-D dispatch in `kokoro/` and the first to hit it. Worth
   a look the next time a result is *identically* zero rather than wrong.

**Tolerances.** Every block against the dump, bounded at 6e-3 (the decoder's,
the same block): 3.4e-5 to 8.9e-5, six of six. Both curves against the dump
and against the CPU path: 2.4e-5 either way. Durations compared as integers,
fifty of fifty unchanged, so the alignment and everything downstream of it are
identical.

**The ladder, measured rather than assumed.** These convolutions are M of 130
or 260 by N of 512 and 256 at K = 3*512 and 3*256 — a third of the decoder's K
— so the rung was re-swept: `conv_reg32x32_w32` 0.35 ms, `32x64_w32` 0.38,
`32x128` 0.54, `reg64` 0.57. The decoder's winner wins again, and wave32 leads
on a fifth geometry (§6.2).

**Where the 0.39 ms of GPU time goes.** conv1 36%, conv2 18%, conv1x1 4% —
58% in the matrix cores — and **32% in the AdaIN reduction**, of which the
`affine` pass alone is 13% for a [2C] reduction over eight chunks that is one
workgroup and pure launch latency. The stacks measure 1 ms of wall clock
against 0.39 ms on the device, so **the other 0.6 ms is the submit and the
fence**, which is S8's finding in a third place and is not worth chasing at
1 ms.

**Left on the table, with its number attached.** T6c is the recurrences and is
now **79 ms of a 115 ms utterance**: the duration encoder's three bidirectional
LSTMs (30 ms), the duration head's one (9), `shared` (22) and the text
encoder's (17). Six of them, each a GEMV at M = 1 that cannot start until the
last one finished — S8's problem in a different model, and S8's answer applies.
The phoneme side is now **66% of an utterance and 96% of it is recurrences**.

'''

content.text:
**T6b is done: the F0/N stacks are on Vulkan, 40 ms → 1 ms, and an utterance is 28.1x real time (was 20.9x).**

```
stage          gpu    (T6a)   cpu (T3)
bert            4ms      4ms     104ms
dur encoder    28ms     28ms      24ms
durations       9ms      9ms       8ms
prosody        26ms     67ms      66ms   shared LSTM 24ms, F0/N stacks 1ms
text encoder   15ms     16ms      15ms
phoneme side   75ms    116ms     222ms   65% of the utterance
vocoder        40ms     40ms    3626ms
total         116ms    156ms    3848ms   28.07x real time, from 20.88x
```

**The instrument came first, and it moved the number.** `SPEECH.md` had carried "~33 ms" for these stacks, inferred by subtraction. Splitting `Prosody` measured **24 ms of recurrence against 40 ms of stacks** — a third of the whole phoneme side. Three lines of `time.Now()` before any kernel.

**Almost all of the work was not writing new code.** These six blocks are `AdainResBlk1d`, the same type `GPUDecoder` has run since T4c. So the stage is a refactor plus plumbing: `kokoro/adainset.go` lifts the block machinery out of `gpudec.go` into a `blockSet` both objects embed (`GPUDecoder` 729 → 322 lines, its numbers unmoved at 59.1 dB / 18.2 dB), and `kokoro/gpuprosody.go` says where inputs come from and outputs go. **One new shader in the whole stage.**

Three findings worth carrying:

- **The third kind of shortcut is no shortcut.** Four of the six blocks keep their channel count, so upstream has no `conv1x1`. On the device that's three dispatches and an fp16 sub-arena that don't happen — the epilogue reads the input in place. It cost one thing: the epilogue had assumed its second operand carried the block's own row stride, true only when the block made it.
- **A 1-wide output is a kernel, not a rung.** The projections are `[260,256] × [256,1]`. A fragment tile is 16 columns wide, so the narrowest GEMM available is 15 columns of zero weight plus a narrow into fp16 for an operand already in fp32. It's on the device for the *boundary*, not the arithmetic: the alternative is fetching the last block's `[260,256]` activation at 210 MB/s, 1.3 ms a curve.
- **`GroupsY` defaults to zero and a zero grid is legal.** The projection dispatched nothing and failed silently — every block correct to 1e-4, both curves exactly 0.0. First 1-D dispatch in `kokoro/`.

Correctness: six of six blocks against the dump at 3.4e-5–8.9e-5 (bound 6e-3); both curves 2.4e-5 against the dump *and* the CPU; fifty of fifty durations unchanged. Ladder re-swept — `conv_reg32x32_w32` wins again at 0.35 ms, wave32 leading on a fifth geometry. Build, vet, gofmt and the full suite are clean.

**T6c is now the whole remaining problem**: 76 ms of a 116 ms utterance in six bidirectional LSTMs, 94% of the phoneme side. Everything else there — ALBERT and the stacks together — is 5 ms.
T6c it is. Starting with what exists — the CPU LSTM, and S8's device answer for the same problem.

attachment.snippet:
1	package kokoro
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"time"
6	)
7	
8	// TextEncoder is the second, shallower path from the phonemes: an embedding,
9	// three 5-tap convolutions with a layer norm and a leaky ReLU, and one
10	// bidirectional LSTM.
11	//
12	// The model reads its input twice — once through ALBERT to decide *how long*
13	// each phoneme lasts and what pitch it carries, and once through here to
14	// decide what it sounds like. This path is the one whose output is expanded
...
16	
17		Embedding *Embedding
18		Convs     []*Conv1D
19		Norms     []*LayerNorm
20		LSTM      *LSTM
21	}
22	
23	// Apply runs the encoder over a token sequence and returns [T, Channels].
24	func (t *TextEncoder) Apply(ids []int, times *ProsodyTimes) (*Mat, error) {
25		x, err := t.Embedding.Rows(ids)
26		if err != nil {
27			return nil, err
28		}
29		for i := range t.Convs {
30			if x, err = t.Convs[i].Apply(x); err != nil {
31				return nil, fmt.Errorf("kokoro: text encoder conv %d: %w", i, err)
32			}
33			if err = t.Norms[i].ApplyInPlace(x); err != nil {
34				return nil, fmt.Errorf("kokoro: text encoder norm %d: %w", i, err)
35			}
36			leakyReLUInPlace(x, 0.2)
37		}
38		t0 := time.Now()
39		out, err := t.LSTM.Apply(x)
40		if times != nil {
41			times.Recurrence += time.Since(t0)
42		}
43		return out, err
44	}

1	package kokoro
2	
3	import (
4		"testing"
5		"time"
6	)
7	
8	// lstmTol is what a recurrence's device path is held to as an rms difference
9	// against the reference dump over the tensor's own rms.
10	//
11	// Looser than the AdaIN blocks' 6e-3 would need to be and tighter than it is,
12	// for a reason worth stating: an LSTM's error does not average out along the
13	// sequence the way a convolution stack's does. Every step's fp16 product
14	// feeds the next step's state through a sigmoid and a tanh, so the question a
15	// bound answers here is whether the *recurrence* is stable, not whether one
16	// dot product is accurate. At 130 steps it measures a few parts in ten
17	// thousand, which says it is.
18	const lstmTol = 3e-3
19	
20	// TestGPULSTM runs the prosody predictor's `shared` recurrence on the device
21	// against the reference dump.
22	//
23	// `shared` is the longest of the six — 130 frames rather than fifty tokens —
24	// so it is the one where a state that decayed slightly wrong would show. It
25	// is also the one whose input the dump records on both sides, which makes it
26	// the only one checkable in isolation without replaying the chain above it.
27	func TestGPULSTM(t *testing.T) {
28		dev, done := newTestDevice(t)
29		defer done()
30		m := loadManifest(t)
31		model := loadModel(t)
32		en := refMat(t, m, "en", true)
33	
34		g, err := NewGPULSTM(dev, model.Predictor.Shared, en.Rows)
35		if err != nil {
36			t.Fatal(err)
37		}
38		defer g.Destroy()
39	
40		got, err := g.Apply(en)
41		if err != nil {
42			t.Fatal(err)
43		}
44		want := refMat(t, m, "shared_out", false)
45		if got.Rows != want.Rows || got.Cols != want.Cols {
46			t.Fatalf("device gives %v, reference has [%d %d]", got, want.Rows, want.Cols)
47		}
48		dv := compare(t, got.Data, want.Data)
49		if dv.Rel() > lstmTol {
50			t.Errorf("shared: relative %.3g (max abs %.3g at %d, rms %.3g)",
51				dv.Rel(), dv.MaxAbs, dv.At, dv.RMS)
52		} else {
53			t.Logf("shared against the dump: relative %.3g", dv.Rel())
54		}
55	
56		// And against the CPU path, which is the stricter comparison: the dump
57		// and the CPU agree to 1e-5, so anything the device gets wrong shows up
58		// here at full size rather than against a reference the host also misses.
59		host, err := model.Predictor.Shared.Apply(en)
60		if err != nil {
61			t.Fatal(err)
62		}
63		dv = compare(t, got.Data, host.Data)
64		if dv.Rel() > lstmTol {
65			t.Errorf("shared against the CPU: relative %.3g", dv.Rel())
66		} else {
67			t.Logf("shared against the CPU: relative %.3g", dv.Rel())
68		}
69	}
70	
71	// TestGPULSTMAll runs all six of the model's recurrences on the device over
72	// the sequences they actually see, and times them against the host.
73	//
74	// All six against one, because they are the same object at three input widths
75	// and two sequence lengths — and because the one that is wrong would be the
76	// one whose weights were staged from the wrong direction, which a single
77	// check of `shared` could not catch.
78	func TestGPULSTMAll(t *testing.T) {
79		dev, done := newTestDevice(t)
80		defer done()
81		m := loadManifest(t)
82		model := loadModel(t)
83		p := model.Predictor
84	
85		en := refMat(t, m, "en", true)
86		dur := refMat(t, m, "dur_encoded", false)
87		cases := []struct {
88			name string
89			l    *LSTM
90			x    *Mat
91		}{
92			{"dur 0", p.TextEncoder.LSTMs[0], refMat(t, m, "dur_norm_0", true)},
93			{"dur 1", p.TextEncoder.LSTMs[1], refMat(t, m, "dur_norm_0", true)},
94			{"dur 2", p.TextEncoder.LSTMs[2], refMat(t, m, "dur_norm_1", true)},
95			{"duration head", p.LSTM, dur},
96			{"shared", p.Shared, en},
97			{"text encoder", model.TextEncoder.LSTM, nil},
98		}
99		// The text encoder's LSTM takes the convolution stack's output, which the
100		// dump records channel-first and at the one input width that is not 640.
101		cases[len(cases)-1].x = refMat(t, m, "te_cnn_2", true)
102	
103		var gpu, cpu time.Duration
104		for _, c := range cases {
105			if c.x.Cols != c.l.In {
106				t.Fatalf("%s: input is %d wide, the LSTM takes %d", c.name, c.x.Cols, c.l.In)
107			}
108			g, err := NewGPULSTM(dev, c.l, c.x.Rows)
109			if err != nil {
110				t.Fatal(err)
111			}
112			if _, err := g.Apply(c.x); err != nil { // warm
113				g.Destroy()
114				t.Fatal(err)
115			}
116			t0 := time.Now()
117			got, err := g.Apply(c.x)
118			if err != nil {
119				g.Destroy()
120				t.Fatal(err)
121			}
122			dg := time.Since(t0)
123			g.Destroy()
124	
125			t0 = time.Now()
126			want, err := c.l.Apply(c.x)
127			if err != nil {
128				t.Fatal(err)
129			}
130			dc := time.Since(t0)
131			gpu, cpu = gpu+dg, cpu+dc
132	
133			dv := compare(t, got.Data, want.Data)
134			if dv.Rel() > lstmTol {
135				t.Errorf("%s: relative %.3g (max abs %.3g at %d)", c.name, dv.Rel(), dv.MaxAbs, dv.At)
136			}
137			t.Logf("%-14s %3d steps, %4d in    relative %.3g    %6.2f ms against %6.2f on the host",
138				c.name, c.x.Rows, c.l.In, dv.Rel(),
139				float64(dg.Microseconds())/1000, float64(dc.Microseconds())/1000)
140		}
141		t.Logf("%-14s                          six recurrences  %6.2f ms against %6.2f, %.1fx",
142			"total", float64(gpu.Microseconds())/1000, float64(cpu.Microseconds())/1000,
143			float64(cpu)/float64(gpu))
144	}
145	
146	// TestGPULSTMProfile prints what the three kinds of dispatch cost: the narrow,
147	// the input projection lifted out of the loop, and one timestep.

150	// fixed cost paid twice per LSTM, and the step is paid 330 times across the
151	// model.
152	func TestGPULSTMProfile(t *testing.T) {
153		dev, done := newTestDevice(t)
154		defer done()
155		model := loadModel(t)
156	
157		for _, c := range []struct {
158			name string
159			l    *LSTM
160			t    int
161		}{
162			{"tokens", model.Predictor.LSTM, 50},
163			{"frames", model.Predictor.Shared, 130},
164		} {

166			if err != nil {

168			}
169			stages, err := g.Profile(c.t)
170			if err != nil {
171				g.Destroy()
172				t.Fatal(err)
173			}
174			var step float64
175			for _, s := range stages {
176				t.Logf("%-8s %-10s %7.4f ms", c.name, s.Kind, s.Time*1000)
177				if s.Kind == "step" {

179				}
180			}
181			t.Logf("%-8s %-10s %7.4f ms over %d steps", c.name, "loop", step*float64(c.t)*1000, c.t)

183		}

49	//
50	// Bidirectional is the structural difference from parakeet, whose prediction
51	// network is causal by construction. Here every recurrence sees the whole
52	// utterance, which is why the phoneme side of this model cannot be streamed
53	// and the vocoder side can.
54	type LSTM struct {
55		In, Hidden int // Hidden is per direction; the output is 2*Hidden wide
56		Fwd, Rev   *LSTMDirection
57	
58		// GPU, when set, runs this recurrence on the device. It is nil by
59		// default: the CPU path above is the reference and stays the reference.
60		//
61		// It hangs off the LSTM rather than off the four objects that own one —
62		// the duration encoder, the duration head, the prosody predictor and the
63		// text encoder — because all four reach their recurrence through
64		// `Apply`, and putting the branch here is the difference between one
65		// change and four signatures (SPEECH.md T6c).
66		GPU *GPULSTM
67	}
68	
69	// Apply runs both directions over a [T, In] activation and returns
70	// [T, 2*Hidden], forward in the first Hidden channels and reverse in the
71	// last — torch's concatenation order.
72	func (l *LSTM) Apply(x *Mat) (*Mat, error) {
73		if x.Cols != l.In {
74			return nil, fmt.Errorf("kokoro: lstm takes %d channels, got %d", l.In, x.Cols)
75		}
76		if l.GPU != nil {
77			return l.GPU.Apply(x)
78		}
79		out := NewMat(x.Rows, 2*l.Hidden)
80		gates := make([]float32, 4*l.Hidden)
81		h := make([]float32, l.Hidden)
82		c := make([]float32, l.Hidden)
83		for t := 0; t < x.Rows; t++ {
84			l.Fwd.step(x.Row(t), h, c, gates)
85			copy(out.Row(t)[:l.Hidden], h)
86		}

python3 - <<'PYEOF'
p='TODO.md'
s=open(p).read()
anchor='### Session 2026-09-15 (twenty-seventh) — stage T6b: the F0/N stacks, and a block that was already written'
new = '''### Session 2026-09-15 (twenty-eighth) — stage T6c: the six recurrences, and a knob that was not the one being turned

**Result: the six bidirectional LSTMs go from 73 ms to 6 — and an utterance
from 116 ms to 53, 28.1x real time to 61.4x. Fifty of fifty durations are
unchanged and both prosody curves agree with the host to 3e-5.**

    stage          gpu    (T6b)   cpu (T3)
    bert            4ms      4ms     104ms
    dur encoder     3ms     28ms      24ms   three bidirectional LSTMs
    durations       1ms      9ms       8ms   one more, and the head
    prosody         2ms     26ms      66ms   shared LSTM 2ms, F0/N stacks 1ms
    text encoder    8ms     15ms      15ms   three convolutions and one LSTM
    phoneme side   17ms     75ms     222ms   32% of the utterance
    vocoder        36ms     40ms    3626ms
    total          53ms    116ms    3848ms   61.44x real time, from 28.07x

    of which the recurrences    6ms     73ms     73ms   12.3x

**The instrument was right this time, and said so before anything was
written.** T6a and T6b had each found the plan wrong by measuring; here the
same three lines of `time.Now()` — threaded through the four stages that own a
recurrence — put **73 ms of a 76 ms phoneme side** in the six LSTMs. 96%.
Everything else on that side, ALBERT and the AdaIN stacks and the
convolutions and the length regulator together, was 3 ms.

**One algebraic move does most of the work.** Torch's step is
`W_ih x_t + W_hh h_{t-1} + b`, and the first term depends on nothing the loop
produces. So `P = X W_ih^T + b` is computed for the whole sequence up front as
**one GEMM with both directions' weights concatenated along N**, and the loop
is left with `W_hh h`. That takes the per-step B operand from
`[4H, In+H]` at 1.8 MB to `[H, 4H]` at 0.5, removes the per-step pass that
would otherwise assemble `[x_t | h_{t-1}]` as an fp16 operand, and leaves the
sequential part small enough to stay MALL-resident for every step of every
LSTM in the model.

**Built:**

- `shaders/kokoro_lstm.comp` — one timestep, both directions, one dispatch.
  Four builds over two knobs.
- `kokoro/gpulstm.go` — `GPULSTM`: a narrow, the input projection, and T
  dispatches, all in one command buffer.
- `LSTM.GPU`, one field, which is how all six call sites changed at once.
- `ProsodyTimes.Recurrence`, printed by `cmd/tts`.
- `kokoro/gpulstm_test.go` — five tests: `shared` against the dump, all six
  against the CPU, the two-knob ladder, the dispatch profile, and the
  durations.

**Five things worth carrying forward:**

1. **The knob was not the one being turned.** A step is 0.5 MB of weights
   against 0.26 MFLOP — 500 bytes a FLOP — so it reads as a bandwidth problem,
   and the first optimisation was the obvious one: spread it from two
   workgroups to eight so fewer bytes go through each CU. **It changed
   nothing**, 12.1 microseconds either way, and sixteen workgroups changed
   nothing either. What the kernel was short of was *outstanding loads*.
   Deepening the unroll from 4 taps to 32 took it from **12.0 microseconds a
   step to 3.7**; past 32 the register pressure takes it back. A recurrence
   has only 4H threads to issue loads from, so depth per thread is the only
   parallelism left — and the `u4` build is kept so the finding stays
   measurable.
2. **Measure the step on the critical path, not alone.** 130 *different* step
   dispatches with barriers cost 11.9 microseconds each; the same 130 with
   barriers off cost 0.53, because they all overlap and hit the same hot
   megabyte. Neither number is the step: the first includes what a serialised
   dispatch costs, the second is a throughput figure for work that cannot be
   thrown at the machine in parallel. A trivial dispatch serialised the same
   way is 1.27 microseconds, which is the floor this stage is 3x above.
3. **A static graph is not a decode loop.** S8 spends three dispatches and a
   host round trip a step because a transducer decides what to do next from
   what it just emitted. Nothing is decided here — the sequence length is
   known before the first dispatch — so the whole recurrence is T+2 dispatches
   in one command buffer, with no fence in the middle. That difference is
   worth more than any kernel in the stage.
4. **The state has to be double-buffered the moment there is more than one
   workgroup.** Band 0 can write `h[0..63]` before band 1 has read it, and two
   workgroups of one dispatch cannot be ordered. The cell state needs no such
   thing: cell i belongs to one band for the whole sequence. This was found by
   reasoning rather than by a wrong answer, which is the good case and is not
   the usual one.
5. **One field beat four signatures.** `LSTM.GPU` hangs off the recurrence
   rather than off the four objects that own one, because all four reach it
   through `Apply`. T6b's instrument had needed a `*ProsodyTimes` threaded
   through three of those signatures; the device path needed none.

**Tolerances.** `shared` against the dump and against the CPU, bounded at
3e-3: 1.02e-4 both ways. All six against the CPU over the sequences they
actually see: 1.0e-4 to 3.8e-4. End to end, **fifty of fifty durations
unchanged**, F0 3.7e-5, energy 2.2e-5, the expanded phoneme features 1.1e-4.

**The ladder.** Over 130 frames: `lstm_c64_u4` 12.0 microseconds a step,
`c128` 4.5, `c64` **3.7**, `c32` 3.8. Bands are worth 0.8 of those 8.3
microseconds and the unroll is worth 7.5.

**Left on the table, with its number attached.** The six recurrences are
6 ms of wall clock over **1.4 ms of GPU time**: the other 3.7 ms is six
readbacks, 776 KB at the 210 MB/s this device reads host-visible memory at,

prediction state does not change and the joints for consecutive frames are
independent, i.e. one GEMM at M = 16 for the price of the M = 1 one. This clip
has only 8 blanks in 46 emissions; a clip with silence in it has many more.

changes every frame's hidden state, so chunking belongs in the design rather

and the score matrices are 1024x1024 per head. It would also bound the
subsampling arena, whose largest tensor is `[4T, 64, 256]` fp32 — 36 MB at 138
frames and 268 MB at 1024. Narrowing that to fp16 halves it *and* halves the
two kernels that are 80% of the subsampling stack, both bandwidth-bound; it
has not been done because the whole stack is 1 ms.

**Smaller, and measured.** `UploadMel` is 1 ms, almost all of it computing
2T-1 rows of sinusoidal position embeddings in float64 on the host — they
depend on nothing but T and could be cached. The encoder's eight per-head
position-score GEMMs are the same shape at different offsets, which is §3.5's
grouped GEMM.

content.text:
**T6c is done: the six bidirectional LSTMs go from 73 ms to 6, and an utterance from 116 ms to 53 — 28.1x real time to 61.4x.** T6 is finished; the phoneme side went 222 ms → 17 ms across the three stages.

```
stage          gpu    (T6b)   cpu (T3)
bert            4ms      4ms     104ms
dur encoder     3ms     28ms      24ms
durations       1ms      9ms       8ms
prosody         2ms     26ms      66ms
text encoder    8ms     15ms      15ms
phoneme side   17ms     75ms     222ms   32% of the utterance
  recurrences   6ms     73ms      73ms     six LSTMs, 12.3x
vocoder        36ms     40ms    3626ms   68% of the utterance
total          53ms    116ms    3848ms   61.44x real time
```

**The instrument agreed with the plan this time** — 73 ms of a 76 ms phoneme side in the six LSTMs, 96%, with ALBERT, the stacks, the convolutions and the length regulator sharing the other 3 ms.

**One algebraic move does most of the work.** Torch's step is `W_ih·x_t + W_hh·h_{t-1} + b`, and the first term depends on nothing the loop produces. So `P = X·W_ihᵀ + b` is one GEMM over the whole sequence with both directions' weights concatenated along N, and the loop keeps only `W_hh·h`. The per-step B operand drops 1.8 MB → 0.5, small enough to stay MALL-resident, and the pass that would assemble `[x_t | h_{t-1}]` stops existing. And because the sequence length is known before the first dispatch, the whole recurrence is T+2 dispatches in **one command buffer** — no fence in the middle, which is the difference from S8's transducer loop.

Three findings worth keeping:

- **The knob was not the one being turned.** A step is 500 bytes a FLOP, so it reads as bandwidth. Spreading it from two workgroups to eight, then sixteen: **12.1 µs either way**. What it was short of was outstanding loads — deepening the unroll from 4 taps to 32 took it to **3.7 µs**. A recurrence has only 4H threads to issue from, so depth per thread is the only parallelism left. The `u4` build ships so the finding stays measurable.
- **Measure the step on the critical path.** 130 step dispatches with barriers cost 11.9 µs each; with barriers off, 0.53 — they overlap and hit the same hot megabyte. The second is a throughput number for work that can't be run in parallel.
- **One field beat four signatures.** `LSTM.GPU` hangs off the recurrence, not the four objects that own one, because all four reach it through `Apply`.

Correctness: all six against the CPU at 1.0e-4 to 3.8e-4; `shared` against the dump at 1.02e-4. End to end, **fifty of fifty durations unchanged**, F0 3.7e-5, energy 2.2e-5. Build, vet, gofmt and the full suite clean; two runs of `cmd/tts` reproduce at 53 ms.

**What's left, with numbers attached.** The six recurrences are 6 ms of wall clock over **1.4 ms of GPU time** — the rest is six readbacks of 776 KB at 210 MB/s. Removing it (T6d) needs no new shader: the AdaLayerNorms are parakeet's LayerNorm kernel with the style affine T6b already computes host-side. With the text encoder's convolutions that's 11 ms of 53. But **the vocoder is 68% of an utterance again**, and the single largest stage in the model is now the **excitation at 15 ms** of float64 phase accumulation on the host — I've written up in `SPEECH.md` why the open question there is whether `HarmonicSource`'s *wrapped* formulation is float32-safe, not whether upstream's 1.3e5-radian accumulator can move.
T6d. First, what the existing kernels can and can't do — strides matter for the concat-as-row-stride trick.

29	//	dEn ─▶ lstm0 ─▶ norm0 ─▶ lstm1 ─▶ norm1 ─▶ lstm2 ─▶ norm2 ─┬─▶ lstm3 ─▶ head ─▶ logits

33	//	                                                            └─▶ gather ─▶ shared ─▶ F0/N

35	//	ids ─▶ embedding ─▶ (conv ─▶ norm ─▶ leaky) x3 ─▶ lstm4 ─▶ t_en
36	//
37	// Two things leave the device. The duration **logits**, [T, 64] and 13 KB,
38	// because rounding a sum of sigmoids is a host decision and every frame count
39	// downstream depends on it; and the text encoder's **t_en**, [T, 512] and
40	// 102 KB, because the vocoder still takes its input from the host. Reading

115	func NewGPUPhonemes(dev *vk.Device, m *Model, frames int) (*GPUPhonemes, error) {
116		g := &GPUPhonemes{

134	// stages the weights.
135	//
136	// The order is forced: the recurrences reserve their own space, this object
137	// reserves what sits between them, and only then does the buffer exist — so
138	// the pipelines, which bind it, are the last thing built.
139	func (g *GPUPhonemes) build(m *Model) error {
140		p := m.Predictor
141		g.hidden = 2 * p.Shared.Hidden
142		g.durPad = roundUp(m.Config.MaxDur, coopMatTile*2)
143	
144		// The recurrences, each reserving its own input projection and state.
145		var err error
146		for i := range g.dur {
147			if g.dur[i], err = newGPULSTM(g.dev, p.TextEncoder.LSTMs[i], g.maxTok, g.arena); err != nil {

149			}
150		}
151		if g.durLST, err = newGPULSTM(g.dev, p.LSTM, g.maxTok, g.arena); err != nil {
152			return fmt.Errorf("kokoro: duration head recurrence: %w", err)
153		}
154		if g.shared, err = newGPULSTM(g.dev, p.Shared, g.frames, g.arena); err != nil {
155			return fmt.Errorf("kokoro: shared recurrence: %w", err)
156		}
157		if g.text, err = newGPULSTM(g.dev, m.TextEncoder.LSTM, g.maxTok, g.arena); err != nil {
158			return fmt.Errorf("kokoro: text encoder recurrence: %w", err)
159		}
160	
161		// This object's own fp32 regions.
162		rows := roundUp(g.maxTok, framePad)
163		g.aDEn = g.arena.reserve(rows * g.hidden)
164		g.aLogits = g.arena.reserve(rows * g.durPad)
165		g.aIdx = g.arena.reserve(roundUp(g.frames, framePad))
166		g.aEn = g.arena.reserve(roundUp(g.frames, framePad) * g.hidden)

180		// fp32 weights: three style affines, three of the text encoder's own, and
181		// its three convolution biases.

190			g.wTEBias[i] = takeW(c)

193		// fp16 weight bank: the duration head, then the three convolutions.
194		halves := 0

The head went back to the host in fp32 and the drift returned to 0.006 frames. A dot product whose output is rounded is not the same kind of tensor as one whose output is added.

Two more worth keeping:

- **A constant input channel is part of the operand, not the data.** Five of six recurrences take `[h | style]` — the same 128 numbers in every row. `SetTail` writes them once into the fp16 A operand, in columns `lstmPad` had already reserved, so torch's `Concat(h, s)` becomes nothing. It also *removed a kernel before it was written*: with the style out of the data, every normalisation runs over a 512-wide row, so AdaLayerNorm is parakeet's LayerNorm with `(1+gamma)`/`beta` computed host-side once per utterance.
- **Read back the shorter tensor.** `t_en` can be expanded on-device and returned as [L, 512], or returned as [T, 512] and expanded on the host. Same gather either way; 102 KB beats 266. At 210 MB/s the *direction* of a gather is a bandwidth decision.

Correctness: link by link against the host at 1.2e-4 to 2.0e-4 (bound 3e-3); curves against the dump at 5.3e-5/3.9e-5; end to end **fifty of fifty durations unchanged**, and the waveform's rms moves 1537.1 → 1537.3. Build, vet, gofmt and every package's tests clean; two runs reproduce at 44–45 ms.

**Where the 1.96 ms goes:** the recurrences' steps are 1.48 ms (76% — `shared` alone is 0.51, being 130 steps to the others' 50), the F0/N stacks 0.20, the text encoder's convolutions 0.076, and nothing else reaches a twentieth of a millisecond.

**Next is T7.** The vocoder is 82% of an utterance again and the largest single stage in the model is the **excitation at 14–15 ms**, 32% of an utterance and nearly twice the whole phoneme side. As I noted in `SPEECH.md`, the open question is whether `HarmonicSource`'s *wrapped* phase formulation is float32-safe — a measurement, not an argument, since it already keeps the phase in cycles rather than upstream's 1.3e5 radians.

# PIPELINE — the z-image-turbo vertical slice

> **PARKED 2026-09-14, and this file is the record of where.** The current
> work is [`SPEECH.md`](SPEECH.md) — the parakeet and kokoro verticals — and
> this slice resumes after them. Nothing below is stale: it is the state the
> pipeline is in, and the three items under "Where the image budget stands"
> are where to pick it up. The short version: an image is **14.26 s**, the DiT
> is **94%** of it, and the only thing left worth more than a percent is the
> **quarter of the WMMA ceiling the seven projections do not reach — 2.6 s**.

> **This file is rewritten, not appended.** It states where the pipeline is
> *now* and what happens next. History belongs in `TODO.md` (session
> handoffs) and `research/` (closed findings); if a paragraph here is about
> the past, it is in the wrong file. Keep it under ~200 lines — it earns a
> few more with each stage that closes, and loses them when a stage's detail
> moves to `research/`.

**Status**: **the target is met, and the block has no layout work left in it.**
`go run ./cmd/zimage -prompt "..."` writes a 1024x1024 PNG in **14.3 s** —
tokenizer, text encoder, 34 DiT blocks over eight denoising steps, VAE, PNG —
and reproduces diffusers' fp32 CPU pipeline to **2.2e-2** of the decoded image.
Two runs agree to 14.18 s and 14.34 s. Every weight is resident: 7.17 GB of
text encoder, 12.54 GB of transformer, 0.30 GB of VAE and 4.90 GB of
activations, 21.9 s to load, and then images cost only their own time.

Stage 9 took the last host arithmetic out of the denoising loop, the patch
embedder and the final layer: **59 ms of CPU a step to 5-10**. Stage 10 then
removed the two dispatches in the block that moved no information — `pack v`
and `narrow ctx`, each of them a tensor read back and written out in the shape
the next kernel wanted — by making them the *store instruction* of the kernel
above: **18 dispatches a block to 16**, 53.17 ms to **51.80**, an image 14.49 s
to **14.26**.

So the whole of what is left is the DiT's arithmetic. The DiT is **94% of an
image**, and inside a block it is 74% GEMM at 73-76% of the WMMA ceiling, 14%
attention and 12% elementwise. Nothing outside it is worth a percent.

**Target**: `prompt → PNG` for Z-Image-Turbo at 1024x1024, 8 steps, fp16.

## Why this exists

Phase 1 — fifteen-plus sessions of microbenchmarks — ended 2026-09-13 with no
convergence criterion (`TODO.md` carries the argument). **The unit of work is
now "a thing that runs", not "an experiment":** a profiler chooses the
optimisation targets, the backlog does not. Stage 4 is what that looks like —
it went looking for the kernel `results/shapes.csv` said would win, found it
the *slowest* in the ladder once the weight and the launch order were what the
memory system wanted, and closed three backlog items on the way without ever
having gone looking for them.

## The model, as the checkpoint actually describes it

Read with `go run ./cmd/inspect models/Z-Image-Turbo/<part>`. These differ
from `bench/modelshapes.go`, which was transcribed from `config.json` by
hand and has gaps that change the arithmetic:

| | |
|---|---|
| DiT blocks | **34**, not 30 — 30 `layers` + 2 `context_refiner` + 2 `noise_refiner` |
| Width / heads | dim 3840, 30 heads, head_dim 128, `qk_norm` on `[128]` |

177 GFLOP in 13.8 ms is **12.9 TFLOP/s** of useful work, i.e. charged for the
tile padding but not for it.

## The graph

Forty dispatches per layer, 960 for the stack, recorded into four command
buffers. Per layer, in order:

    norm ff1 → gemm ff1.linear1 → silu → gemm ff1.linear2 → x += 0.5·y
    norm attn → gemm q, k, v → pack q(+bias_u), k, v → bias_v narrow
               → gemm rel_k → narrow rel_k → 8 × gemm pos → rel shift
               → attention → gemm o → x += y
    norm conv → gemm conv.pw1 → glu → dwconv → gemm conv.pw2 → x += y
    norm ff2 → gemm ff2.linear1 → silu → gemm ff2.linear2 → x += 0.5·y
    norm out (in place, fp32)

Eleven of those are the DiT's GEMM (`shaders/dit_gemm.comp`) and one is its
attention kernel; the other seven shaders are new and small. The profile at
138 frames, summed over 24 layers:

| kind | n | total | share |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gemm ff1.linear1` / `ff2.linear1` | 48 | 4.0 ms | 29% |
| `gemm ff1.linear2` / `ff2.linear2` | 48 | 4.0 ms | 29% |
=== t4 ===
    with     A[t, j*C + c] = x[t + j*d - p, c]

so the A address is the ordinary one **plus `j*(d*lda)`**, and because C is a
power of two, j and c are a shift and a mask of the K index. One 16-wide
fragment therefore lies entirely inside one tap. `A_CONV=1` is twelve lines
in `dit_gemm.comp`: **the im2col is an addressing rule, not a pass**, so a
dilated convolution is one dispatch with no packing and no accumulate flag.
The padding is in the data — a 32-frame zero border at each end of the fp16
arena, with `inOff` at row `border - p` — which is stage 8's conv2d trick one
dimension down, and it leaves the kernel branchless. Every existing build of
`dit_gemm.comp` is byte-for-byte unchanged. **The eight blocks went from
2669 ms to 6.9 ms, 22.4 TFLOP/s.**

Two things are free because they are per utterance, not per frame. Each
AdaIN's `fc` is a `[2C, 128]` projection of one style vector, so the host
computes gamma and beta once and 48 of the 70 `fc` layers leave the graph.
And `conv1`'s bias cancels identically inside the AdaIN that follows it —
dropping all three in a block moves the output by 2.7e-7 relative, against
0.031 for the same experiment on `conv2`, whose output reaches the residual
add.

**AdaIN reduces down a column and is still coalesced**, because the workgroup
is laid out across channels rather than along the column: 256 threads cover
`256/C` row groups, so a wave's addresses are one contiguous run of a row.
The ladder's winner is `reg32x64_w32` at both rates by 1.10-1.28x, which is
§6.2's wave32 result holding on a fourth set of shapes.

so the A address is the ordinary one **plus `j*(d*lda)`**, and because C is a
power of two, j and c are a shift and a mask of the K index. One 16-wide
fragment therefore lies entirely inside one tap. `A_CONV=1` is twelve lines
in `dit_gemm.comp`: **the im2col is an addressing rule, not a pass**, so a
dilated convolution is one dispatch with no packing and no accumulate flag.
The padding is in the data — a 32-frame zero border at each end of the fp16
arena, with `inOff` at row `border - p` — which is stage 8's conv2d trick one
dimension down, and it leaves the kernel branchless. Every existing build of
`dit_gemm.comp` is byte-for-byte unchanged. **The eight blocks went from
2669 ms to 6.9 ms, 22.4 TFLOP/s.**

Two things are free because they are per utterance, not per frame. Each
AdaIN's `fc` is a `[2C, 128]` projection of one style vector, so the host
computes gamma and beta once and 48 of the 70 `fc` layers leave the graph.
And `conv1`'s bias cancels identically inside the AdaIN that follows it —
dropping all three in a block moves the output by 2.7e-7 relative, against
0.031 for the same experiment on `conv2`, whose output reaches the residual
add.

**AdaIN reduces down a column and is still coalesced**, because the workgroup
is laid out across channels rather than along the column: 256 threads cover
`256/C` row groups, so a wave's addresses are one contiguous run of a row.
The ladder's winner is `reg32x64_w32` at both rates by 1.10-1.28x, which is
§6.2's wave32 result holding on a fourth set of shapes.

content.text:
Fresh numbers on all three, plus the measured ceilings from `IDEAS.md` §0 (these were measured on this chip, not extrapolated).

## Where the three verticals are

| | workload | wall clock | real-time factor | load |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **STT** (parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3) | 11.0 s of 16 kHz audio | **44 ms** | **250x** | 1.1 s |
| **TTS** (Kokoro-82M) | 3.25 s of 24 kHz audio | **44 ms** | **74x** | 0.16 s |
| **Image** (Z-Image-Turbo) | 1024², 8 steps | **14.26 s** | — | 21.9 s |

## The machine's measured ceilings

| Ceiling | Peak | Best kernel in this repo |
|---|---|---|
| DRAM bandwidth | 236 GB/s (92% of the 256 GB/s bus) | 239 GB/s — **saturated** |
| MALL (32 MiB) | 805 GB/s copy / 965 read | 805 GB/s — **saturated** |
| WMMA fp16→fp32 | 55.5 TFLOP/s | 42.0 TFLOP/s (**76%**) |
| Vector FP32 FMA | 22.9 TFLOP/s | — |

76% of the WMMA peak is the practical ceiling; nothing reaches 55.5.

## How close each one is — and they're in three different places

**Image generation is at the ceiling.** The DiT is 94% of an image, and inside a block 74% of the time is GEMM running at **73–76% of the WMMA ceiling** — i.e. at the best kernel this repo has. The remaining headroom is the quarter the seven projections don't reach, worth ~2.6 s of the 14.26. This vertical is compute-bound and nearly done; the next real gain would have to come from quantisation, not scheduling.

**STT is bound by the host, not the GPU.** The encoder does 177 GFLOP in 13.8 ms — 12.9 TFLOP/s, **23% of peak / 31% of the practical ceiling** — and it's only 39% of the clip. The **front end is 48%**: 21 ms of float64 FFT on the CPU, untouched since S3 because it used to be 0.8%. Decode is 12% and is round trips, 118 µs an emission over 46 submits. Put the front end on the device and this goes to roughly **24 ms, ~460x**.

**TTS is three problems at once.** Of 44 ms:

| | time | what binds it |
|---|---|---|
| excitation | 14 ms | **host float64 DSP** — not on the GPU at all |
| generator | 12 ms | compute, **22.4 TFLOP/s = 40% of peak, 53% of practical** |
| tail | 8 ms | bandwidth |
| phoneme side | 8 ms | **latency** — 1.96 ms of GPU time in 8 ms of wall |
| decoder | 1 ms | — |

The phoneme side is the interesting one: after T6a–T6d it's 222 ms → 8 ms, but only 1.96 ms of that is the GPU doing work. The rest is two readbacks, ALBERT's readback, and four submits. It's running at a **~25% duty cycle** and at a fraction of a percent of any arithmetic ceiling — because a recurrence has no parallelism to give. Moving the excitation to the device would take TTS to roughly **31 ms, ~105x**.

## The short version

- **Image**: at the practical WMMA ceiling. ~18% left on the table.
- **STT**: the GPU half is at ~31% of practical; the pipeline is half host FFT. ~45% left.
- **TTS**: the generator is at ~53% of practical, but a third of the utterance is host float64 and a fifth is dispatch latency on work that's inherently serial. ~30% left.

The pattern across all three: **every remaining win is a boundary, not a kernel.** Host float64 in two of them, round trips in the third's decode loop, and 2.6 s of tile efficiency in the image DiT. The only place arithmetic is still the answer is quantisation, which is what `GOALS.md`'s Qwen3-Next vertical will force.
